disposition_reason: Tables 3 and 4 print mean ± SD and range of 13 elements, including As, Cd, Pb, Ni, Cr and Al (µg/kg wet weight), in beef and pork cuts bought in Zagreb in 2020.

study.design: Retail survey of beef (84) and pork (70) cuts with dietary exposure and risk characterization
study.market: Various butcher shops, grocery stores and supermarkets at different locations in Zagreb, Croatia
study.lod_text: LOD (Table 2): Al 0.008, Cu 0.003, Fe 0.002, Mg 0.096, Mn 0.006, Ni 0.006, Se 0.009, Zn 0.05 mg/kg; As 3, Cd 2, Cr 5, Mo 5, Pb 2 µg/kg; footnotes: As meat/kidney 1.3/1.4, Cd 0.7/1.0, Pb 0.7/1.7 µg/kg
study.qa: DORM-4 fish protein CRM recoveries 93.6-117.8%; spiked samples for Al, Mg, Mn, Mo (95.5-112%)

unresolved: Sampling text lists 'but' cuts (14 beef, 10 pork) while Tables 3-4 label the row 'loin'; the table label is used.
Table 3 pork first row is labelled 'Cu' instead of 'P loin'.
Cd values printed as '<1.3' for beef loin, neck, shoulder and pork loin, while the Cd LOD for meat is 0.7 µg/kg (Table 2 footnote b); 1.3 µg/kg is the As LOD for meat.
Pork fat Fe range printed '222–0.58' mg/kg (impossible); pork loin Al SD printed 2775 µg/kg against a 145-757 µg/kg range.
Means are computed only from results above LOD (Section 2.6), so they overstate the product mean where non-detects occurred; detection counts are not printed.
